title: Air India Overhauls Pilot Careers With Common Seniority, New Pay as Fleet Triples
excerpt: Tata Group says 'overwhelming majority' of pilots have accepted the revised compensation package as Air India Group grows from 100 to 300 aircraft with 600 more on order.
body:
• Air India has rolled out a revamped Employee Value Proposition for its 5,000-plus pilots across Air India and Air India Express, covering enhanced pay, a common seniority framework, and new career progression pathways.
  • Under the new framework, Air India Express becomes the primary pathway for command upgrades — senior first officers seeking captaincy must serve there before progressing to Air India and widebody flying.
  • The airline says an "overwhelming majority" of pilots have accepted the new terms, though Air India Express pilots have raised concerns about income predictability and leave policies.
  • The restructuring comes as the Air India Group has tripled its fleet from about 100 to nearly 300 aircraft since the 2022 Tata acquisition, with orders for 600 more including 80 widebody planes.

A Group-Wide Restructuring

Tata Group's Air India has launched a sweeping overhaul of pilot compensation and career pathways as it integrates operations across Air India and Air India Express, according to an internal email reviewed by The Hindu BusinessLine.

Air India's Senior Vice-President for Flight Operations, Captain Manish Uppal, told pilots in late August that an "overwhelming majority" had accepted the revised compensation and benefits package, which the airline has branded as a refreshed Employee Value Proposition.

The package includes enhanced pay, new career progression routes, and what the airline describes as measures to improve pilots' quality of life — a significant undertaking for a group that now employs over 5,000 pilots across its two carriers.

Common Seniority Across Two Airlines

The most significant structural change is a common seniority framework spanning Air India and Air India Express. Under the new system, Air India Express will serve as the primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades on narrowbody aircraft.

Pilots who achieve command experience at Air India Express can then progress to Air India and pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. Senior first officers moving to Air India Express for Boeing 737 command upgrades receive a one-time bonus of Rs 10 lakh. Existing Air India Express commanders on the 737 fleet receive Rs 21 lakh spread over three years.

Upon command upgrade, pilots must serve at an Air India Express base for at least two years — extendable by six months — before choosing a preferred posting, according to sources cited by PTI.

Better Pay, But With Conditions

The revised compensation guarantees pay for 40 hours of block flying time, with enhanced allowance rates for additional hours. Training compensation has been increased and linked to fleet-average flying hours. Pilots supporting the growing Boeing 737 fleet at Air India Express receive a separate fleet allowance.

Relocation support has also been enhanced, covering temporary accommodation, household goods, incidental expenses, and relocation leave.

However, the restructuring has not been universally welcomed. Air India Express pilots have raised concerns about income predictability, arguing that the guaranteed 40-hour base is a reduction from the 70 hours guaranteed before the pandemic. They contend that a temporary Covid-era cut should not become permanent, and that tying much of their pay to actual monthly flying hours leaves take-home compensation at the mercy of the airline's rostering decisions.

"The new framework has been mooted amid intense competition among airlines for hiring senior pilots, attrition and also lesser flying hours at present."

— Senior Air India Group pilots, quoted by PTI

Why Now: The Fleet Has Tripled

The urgency behind the restructuring reflects the scale of Air India's transformation under Tata ownership. Since the 2022 acquisition, the group has grown from about 100 aircraft to nearly 300 and placed orders for 600 new planes, including 80 widebody aircraft. The airline has invested in pilot training infrastructure, including an aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators and a flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.

The global pilot shortage adds competitive pressure. Middle Eastern carriers have historically offered salary packages well above Indian standards, and the post-Covid boom in aviation has intensified the scramble for experienced captains. IndiGo, India's largest airline by market share, has been on its own recruitment drive. Air India needs its career pathway and compensation to be compelling enough to stem attrition and attract the crews required for its expanding fleet.

What's Next

Captain Uppal described the revised package as "only the beginning," telling pilots the group would continue to strengthen its proposition. For Air India, the test will be whether a common seniority framework across two carriers with distinct fleet types and operational cultures can hold together as both airlines grow simultaneously. For pilots weighing their options, the question is whether the new career pathway and pay structure match the promises of a carrier that is still losing money even as it scales.
nri_angle: Air India's transformation under Tata ownership directly affects flight options, service quality, and fares for the millions of NRIs who fly the carrier between India and global destinations.
